summary: Sven Wittemann is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed an MA at the International Buddhist College from around 2012 to 2014, supervised by Kapila Abhayawansa.

Swami Siddheswarananda (1897–1957) worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the University of Madras from circa 1916 to 1920 and held a post with the Ramakrishna Order from around 1920 to 1957.

Syed Ali Bilgrami (1853–1911) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at the University of Lucknow, IIT Roorkee, and the University of London, he worked for the Government of Hyderabad (~1879–1901) and was Reader in Marathi at Cambridge (1902).

Syed Hasan Askari (1901–1990) specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Zila School Chapra, Langat Singh College, and Patna University, he served as a professor at Patna University (~1934–1961) and Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1968–1971).
Syed Nawab Ali worked in history and archaeology. He served as Professor of Persian at Baroda College and as Principal of Bahauddin College.
Sylvain Brocquet is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the École Normale Supérieure in 1980 and held a post at Aix-Marseille University.

Sylvain Lévi (1863–1935) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at Lycée Charlemagne and EPHE, he held chairs at EPHE (~1886–1935), the University of Paris (~1889–1894), and Collège de France (1894–1935).
Sze-bong Tso works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a PhD from the Australian National University (1977–1982), supervised by Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana.
Søren Sørensen (1848–1902) was an Indologist. He held positions at Herlufsholm School from 1876 to 1878 and at the University of Copenhagen from circa 1887 until 1902.

T. Chandrasekharan was an Indology scholar who studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He succeeded T. R. Chintamani and served as Professor of History of Sanskrit Language and Literature at The Madras Sanskrit College.

T. Griffith Foulk studied Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, completing a PhD at the University of Michigan (~1980–1987) under Luis Oscar Gómez. He taught as an assistant professor at Michigan (~1987–1995) and Sarah Lawrence College (~1995).

T. R. Chintamani was an Indologist who studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Manager and Correspondent for the Journal of Oriental Research, Madras (1927) and as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras (~1930–1943).

T. R. V. Murti (1902–1986) was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned a D.Litt. from Banaras Hindu University under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, later holding professorships at Oxford (1949–1950), BHU (~1953–1967), and McMaster University (~1970–1972).
T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar worked in Indology and philosophy. He served as Principal of The Madras Sanskrit College and as Professor of Advaita Vedānta at Banaras Hindu University.

T. V. Venkatachala Sastry (born 1933) is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He held academic posts at Osmania University from circa 1959 to 1968 and at the University of Mysore from circa 1968 to 1994.

T. Venkatacharya was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He held positions at the Istituto Italiano per il Medio ed Estremo Oriente and served as a professor in the Department of East Asian Studies at the University of Toronto (~1967–1994).

Tadao Yoshikawa (born 1937) specializes in Sinology, history, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Kyoto University (~1956–1965), he became a professor there (~1984–2000), later holding professorships at Ryukoku University (~2000–2002) and Hanazono University (~2002).

Tadashi Inoue (1929–2014) worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1953), he taught at Bukkyo University, Kyoto University of the Arts, and served as professor at Nara University (~1985–1999).

Tadashi Tani (born 1941) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Waseda, Vienna, and Kyoto under Yuichi Kajiyama. He was a professor at Kochi College (~1986–1997) and lectured at Ryukoku, Hanazono, Bukkyo, and Kobe Women's universities.
Tadashi Toda is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under teachers Keiki Higashimoto and Kogen Mizuno.
